answer: Correlated failure betrays clones: copies share code and hosts, so errors pile on one dune like wind-driven sand, while honest agents scatter like a nebula, each miss bent by a prism of different training. Steps: graders seed rare canary tasks; two agents returning the same exotic wrong answer form a cluster; each forfeits a 50-token bond unless it shows a distinct model and host. Cost: one strike burns 200 clones x 50 = 10,000 tokens; going clean costs $30/mo per model = $6,000 monthly. Like an examiner finding twenty identical wrong answers to one trap question: a shared answer sheet.
